课程简介（中文）

本课程为泰语入门课程，面向无泰语基础或泰语基础较少的学生。课程介绍泰语语音、声调及文字系统的基本特点，并围绕日常交际情境学习基础词汇、常用表达和基本句型。通过听、说、读、写相结合的课堂练习，帮助学生建立基础泰语沟通能力，同时初步了解泰国社会与文化。

课程简介（英文）

This introductory course is designed for students with little or no prior knowledge of Thai. It introduces the Thai sound, tone, and writing systems, together with basic vocabulary, expressions, and sentence patterns for everyday communication. Through integrated listening, speaking, reading, and writing practice, students develop foundational communicative skills while gaining basic awareness of Thai society and culture.

教学目标

The course aims to establish a foundation in Thai language knowledge and basic communication. By the end of the course, students should be able to recognize and produce basic Thai sound system, and use common vocabulary and sentence patterns related to personal information and everyday situations. Students will develop basic listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills while also gaining intercultural awareness through the study of language in its Thai social and cultural contexts.

教学方式

The course adopts a student-centered and communicative approach, emphasizing active participation and meaningful language use. Interactive activities, including situational dialogues, pair and group work, classroom games, task-based activities, and role-plays, provide students with frequent opportunities to immediately apply newly learned Thai vocabulary, expressions, pronunciation, and language skills in practical or simulated communicative situations. A comfortable and supportive classroom atmosphere is maintained to encourage students to experiment with the language, interact with their peers, and gradually develop confidence and competence in using Thai for communication.

教学内容与进度安排

Week 1 – Introduction and Greetings
Introduction to Thai language and culture; Thai greetings and wai; expressions for greeting, thanking, and apologizing; self-introduction, names and nicknames; brief introduction to the Thai alphabet and sound system.

Week 2 – Getting to Know Others
Asking and answering personal information, including nationality, occupation, university, faculty, and hometown; introduction to Thai initial consonant sounds.

Week 3 – People, Things and Family
Introducing and describing people and objects; asking what something is and what it is called; family members, possession, and existence; Thai ending consonant sounds.

Week 4 – Places and Locations
Asking and describing where people live or work; describing the location of people and objects; prepositions of place; buildings, rooms, and floors; describing places and expressing alternatives.

Week 5 – Review and Thai Vowel System
Review and practice of previous content; Thai vowel sounds, including short and long vowels and diphthongs.

Week 6 – Numbers and Quantities
Numbers; age; telephone numbers; family-related quantities; basic classifiers and expressions of possession.

Week 7 – Questions, Preferences and Abilities
Yes/no and confirmation questions; Thai tones; expressions related to wants, preferences, completed actions, and abilities.

Week 8 – Review and Midterm Assessment
Review and integrated practice of the Thai sound system and communicative content covered during the first half of the course; midterm assessment.

Week 9 – Time, Dates and Daily Routines
Asking and telling time; days, months, and years; asking and talking about daily routines.

Week 10 – Opinions, Numbers and Quantities
Expressing basic opinions; larger numbers; asking about price, amount, and quantity.

Week 11 – Shopping and Everyday Requests
Describing clothing and products, including color, size, and material; shopping expressions; asking for help and permission.

Week 12 – Food and Ordering
Ordering food and drinks; food classifiers; specifying orders; describing tastes; related Thai food and festival culture.

Week 13 – Restaurants and Locations
Restaurant communication and role-play; asking and explaining where people, objects, and places are; expressing distance.

Week 14 – Directions and Navigation
Asking for and giving directions; describing routes and locations; map-based and situational practice.

Week 15 – Integrated Language Practice and Review
Thai song and listening activities; integrated communicative practice; comprehensive review; final project preparation.

Week 16 – Final Project and Final Assessment
Final project presentation and final examination.
